# Encoding and Decoding Strategy in `robjc`

This document outlines the internal encoding and decoding mechanisms of the `robjc` object system. It is intended for framework contributors, advanced users, or developers who wish to define custom encoders or decoders.

---

## §1 Overview

The `robjc` framework provides Objective-C-inspired full OOP serialization for R objects. It distinguishes between standard framework classes and user-defined classes using class name and version resolution. The system supports recursive object structure encoding and full restoration via embedded metadata.

---

## §2 Class Architecture (Objective-C Style Syntax)

```objc
@interface RSClassRegistry : RSSingleton {
  list std_classes; // character vector of class names
}
- (BOOL) isStandardClass(character klass_name);
@end

@interface RSClassEncoder : RSModule <RSEncoderProtocol> {
  RSMutableDictionary *class_store;
  list visited_env;
  boolean status_frozen;
}
- (RSInstanceMap *) encodingContainer(id obj);
- (void) encodeObject(id obj);
- (RSDictionary *) finalize(void);
- (RSDictionary *) lockedData(void);
- (void) refresh(void);
@end

@interface RSClassDecoder : RSModule <RSDecoderProtocol> {
  RSDictionary *class_store;
  list unresolved;
}
- (void) loadEncodedData(RSDictionary *dict);
- (void) resolveClassesWithDictionary(RSDictionary *replacement);
- (void) unpackTo(environment target);
@end

@interface RSClassReference : RSKeyValuePair {
  RSString *classID;
  RSInstanceMap *instanceMap;
}
@end

@interface RSInstanceMap : RSKeyValuePair {
  RSWrappedClass *wrappedClass;
  RSSet *objects;
}
@end
```

---

## §3 Encoding Logic

- `RSClassEncoder` traverses object graphs and records class-instance mappings.
- Uses a `mark-and-store` strategy: already visited objects are skipped.
- Each robjc-serializable object must implement `objectsForEncoding()`, which returns a list of child instances.
- `lockInstance()` collects all reachable objects and their class trees.
- The encoded result is a dictionary of `RSClassReference`, each pointing to `RSInstanceMap`.

---

## §4 Decoding Logic

- `RSClassDecoder` loads the encoded metadata (`RSDictionary`) and uses `classID()` strings to match runtime class definitions.
- Standard classes are resolved via `RSClassRegistry`.
- User-defined classes must be supplied in a `class_map` (a dictionary of classID → R6Class object).
- After resolving, `RSObject$resolveClassWith()` replaces the internal class reference.

If class resolution fails for some classIDs, the decoder will issue a warning and mark them as unresolved. This does not interrupt execution.

---

## §5 Example Workflow

```r
# Saving a robjc-compatible object
robjc_save_rds(my_object, file = "data.rds")

# Later, restoring with optional user-defined class mapping
custom_map <- RSDictionary$new(
  keys = list(RSString$stringWith("MyClass_1.0")),
  objects = list(MyClass)
)

restored <- robjc_read_rds("data.rds", class_map = custom_map)
```

- The function `objectsForEncoding()` should be implemented in all custom classes that reference other robjc objects.
- If a class is not resolvable, a warning will list the missing class IDs.

---

## §6 Notes

- The `.__rs_encoded_data__` object is automatically removed after decoding.
- The system supports full recursive encoding and type-safe restoration of object graphs.
- If you implement your own encoder or decoder, be sure to consult this structure.
